description:
T1 – Large Silver Birch

Proposed Works:
• Remove dead, weak or crossing branches
• Thin crown by approx. 10%
• Crown lift to 3.4m

Justification:
The tree contains scattered deadwood and several crossing or weak branches which present a minor hazard and inhibit healthy crown development. Thinning by 10% is a light, selective intervention intended to improve internal light penetration and air flow without altering the overall form. A lift to 3.4m provides appropriate clearance for the garden, reduces shading, and improves access beneath the canopy. Works follow the minimum necessary intervention recommended under BS3998.
Finished Height: No change to overall height.
Finished Spread: No significant change – natural spread retained.


T2 – Silver Birch (adjacent to garage)

Proposed Works:
• Remove limb overhanging garage back to main stem
• Crown reduction back to previous reduction points

Justification:
The limb directly overhanging the garage presents an avoidable structural risk and should be removed to prevent future damage. Returning the canopy to previous reduction points ensures proportional regrowth management, controls lateral spread away from structures, and maintains an even crown outline. Works are minimal, appropriate to its location, and in line with previous management cycles.
Finished Height: 5m
Finished Spread: 3m.


T3 – Yew
Proposed Works:
• Reduce height by approx. 2m (remaining below guttering)
• Trim hard to tidy and contain shape

Justification:
The Yew has become oversized relative to the adjacent building, with growth now interfering with guttering and upper brickwork. A 2m reduction prevents property contact, reduces shading, and improves long-term manageability. Yew tolerates reduction well, and shaping restores a compact form consistent with past maintenance. Works comply with BS3998, ensuring cuts remain to suitable growth points.
Finished Height: 4m
Finished Spread: 3m .


T4 – Holly
Proposed Works:
• Fell to ground level / section dismantle

Justification:
The Holly has outgrown its position and conflicts with surrounding planting and structural features. Removal is the most suitable way forward, as pruning alone would not adequately mitigate the encroachment or restore an appropriate size. Felling prevents future shading, root spread, and structural interference. Removal complies with BS3998 best practice.
